collection.name: Chessmaster Grandmaster Edition
collection.review: Chessmaster Grandmaster Edition is a very good educational tool for new chess players. The best part of it is easily Josh Waitzkins academy, which is both informative and enjoyable. Other than that its very similar to previous chessmaster games. You will want to come back to chessmaster for more advanced classes, but to actually play chess online you should consider something like chess.com (for beginners-intermediate) or internet chess club (for the pros).

collection.name: Streets of Rage 2
collection.review: Streets of Rage 2 is a very hard game to rate. It was one of those games that I played in the store when I was a kid and for its time it was very impressive! Younger gamers that want a cool game by todays standards should stay away, its a very old title that unfortunately havent stood the test of time.

collection.name: Out of This World
collection.review: There are two good things with this game. The graphics and animation were amazing for its time and still look good, especially with the higher resolution. Secondly, the port to iphone/ipad is good and it goes better than I thought it would to tap our hero along the screens. Unfortunately the gameplay is horrible. You will die alot without any warning. Fortunately the game is very short so you will be able to finish before your IPhone is flushed down the toilet in frustration!

collection.name: Alone in the Dark
collection.review:
The first game I played that made me genuinely scared! Animation was at top quality for its time. A gaming classic that I will always remember!

5 stars for nostalgia value. 1 star if you try to play it now, time has not been kind to this game. So it ends up at three stars.

collection.name: Alone in the Dark 3
collection.review: The last game in the original Alone in the Dark trilogy, with a Wild West setting. As the previous games its a solid game with a nice story and some good scares. Unfortunately it doesn't bring anything new to the table either.

collection.name: Alone in the Dark 2
collection.review: A solid followup to the groundbreaking first game. The story is better and more developed in this one, but I remember that it was frustratingly hard at times. The scare factor is also slightly lower.

collection.name: Portal
collection.review: Portal was true innovation when it came out, I had never seen any game like it. In the beginning levels are really easy, so people can understand the concept of portals I guess. But later the game picks up, and in the later chambers I actually got stuck a couple of times. The ending is also action packed and satisfying. Its a short game but well worth your time.

collection.name: Team Fortress 2
collection.review: Team Fortress 2 is the best multiplayer FPS I've played. Most of my gaming life I've avoided these games like the plague, since I suck at it and also generally dont see the point of just killing each other over and over. So its kind of revolutionary that I give a game like this 4 stars. But its funny, they keep stats of just about everything, they got lots of fun gaming modes, a big range of classes that play very differently and beautiful graphics. If you, like me, dont like multiplayer FPS:es you should still give TF2 a try since its free! You might even start to like it. If you're a fan of the genre you've probably play countless hours already.

collection.name: Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Restoration of Erathia
Heroes of Might and Magic III: Armageddon's Blade
Heroes of Might and Magic III: The Shadow of Death
Wing Commander
collection.review: A classic game that's still fun to play. One of my favourites back in the day so I might be biased. Missions can be a bit monotonus but it doesnt matter much when combat is this much fun! Use a joystick if you have one!

collection.name: Wing Commander II: Vengeance of the Kilrathi
Ultima VII: Part Two - Serpent Isle
Ultima VII: The Forge of Virtue
Ultima VII: Part Two - Serpent Isle: The Silver Seed
Ultima IV: Quest of the Avatar
Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic
collection.review:
This review covers the PC version from Steam on a Win7 64bit system.
The game itself is 5 star worthy, even after all these years. It feels completely like Star Wars, even more so than The Old Republic MMO in some ways. The story is captivating and made me not bother much about the dated graphics. It seems that the PC version have problems running on modern systems though. Initially I couldnt get it to run and it only started properly after I disabled the movie sequences. Which is a shame, since they are very good. On my old XP system the game runs fine though.

collection.name: Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II - The Sith Lords
Leisure Suit Larry 5: Passionate Patti Does a Little Undercover Work
Leisure Suit Larry 6: Shape Up or Slip Out!
Leisure Suit Larry: Love for Sail!
Leisure Suit Larry III: Passionate Patti in Pursuit of the Pulsating Pectorals
Leisure Suit Larry 2: Goes Looking for Love (in Several Wrong Places)
Leisure Suit Larry in the Land of the Lounge Lizards

Heroes Chronicles: Warlords of the Wasteland
Heroes Chronicles: Conquest of the Underworld
Heroes Chronicles: Clash of the Dragons
Prince of Persia: The Sands of Time
Prince of Persia: The Two Thrones
Septerra Core: Legacy of the Creator
Borderlands
collection.review: A shooter in a Mad Max world with RPG elements like quests and itemization thrown into the mix. An ok game, but nothing that I wanted to play for a very long time. The story is weak. I found myself skipping quest text and I'm a guy that usually reads them, even in World of Warcraft. The best thing with Borderlands is that its easy to set up a co-op game and go shooting with a friend. A very annoying thing though is that its not possible to abandon quests! After joining a few random groups my log was cluttered with quests that I couldnt finish in my level range anyway. And that made it hard to find the quests I actually wanted to do. To summarize: playing Borderlands single-player is boring, but the co-op can be fun!

collection.name: Master of Orion II: Battle at Antares
Dungeon Siege III
collection.review: Overall a disappointment. I find that controls on the PC are awful and its not possible to remap the keys. The story is boring and doesnt stand out at all and there are almost no exploration possibilities whatsoever. Graphics and sound are ok, but nothing extraordinary. All female characters walk around with double d boobs and pushup cleavages. I personally find laughable and that it takes away credibility from the game, but each to their own I guess. Final point is, if you really want to play Dungeon Siege 3, do it on a console to get the superior controls.

collection.name: The Book of Unwritten Tales: The Critter Chronicles
realMyst
collection.review: Myst is a great game and a classic, but I gave it an average grade since I prefer to play it the "slide show" way. If you're more into free roaming you should grab the masterpiece edition of this one.

collection.name: Batman: Arkham Asylum
collection.review:
This is simply a very good game, worth all the hype its received. Voice acting is fantastic, both Batman and the Joker are perfect and add to the experience. Gameplay is varied and good, its fun to fight like a superhero and take out thugs one by one. Scarecrows world is also good and also provide a bit of backstory. There are a couple of sections that are dull though (I'm looking at you, Killer Croc).
As a whole I found it to be a very good game, even though I didnt care much about Batman before playing it!

collection.name: The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Blood and Wine
The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt - Hearts of Stone
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War - Winter Assault
Warhammer 40,000: Dawn of War - Dark Crusade
Assassin's Creed Brotherhood
collection.review: The third title in this fantastic series still oozes quality. One of the main attractions in an Assassin's Creed game is to explore the cities and Rome is full of interesting locations. Hideouts are still very fun to beat and explore! The single player campaign is solid, even if its slighty less engaging this time around. What I find really impressive is that so much of the historical facts are accurate and seamlessly woven into the story. Graphics are even better now, with a weather system in place that feels very effective. Fighting is also improved, its good fun to rack up execution streaks even if it almost gets too easy. Other new additions include tower capturing and recruitment of assassins. But the best new addition is the cool multiplayer! I really like that being stealthy is just as important as racking up kills.

collection.name: Assassin's Creed II
collection.review: This was a game that I played in less a week even though my game time came up to 36 hours. I just couldnt stop playing all the captivating missions! Gameplay has improved alot on the original. I find that the best new addition are the Assassin's Tombs. They are just great fun to explore and those who loved the Prince of Persia games will feel right at home. Solving puzzles from Subject 16 is also very fun and a good addition. My PC version included the two DLC's that were originally sold as separate expansions but here they are included into the game. I didnt like this, since the drop in production quality really shows. Other than that, everything is great!

collection.name: Assassin's Creed Revelations
collection.review:
Assassin's Creed Revelations is a good game, even though the single player game story feels weaker this time around. There is no real antagonist, and it doesnt feel like Ezio finds out anything of great importance. But for those who have played the first Assassins Creed its nice to find out more about Altair. Gameplay is still very good and I experienced no bugs or glitches. I only had to do den defense once and had no issues with it at all, they must have patched it since launch. Desmonds sequences are ok. It feels like a separate game altogether though and the Subject 16 puzzles from the previous games were a better fit for Assassin's Creed in my opinion. The already excellent multiplayer game has been improved with story elements and some nice new modes. Overall I really enjoyed the MP, even more so than single player. The death matches were very enjoyable. Its almost the same as Wanted but the maps are smaller and there is only an indicator that shows when the target is in sight.
Overall this game is a nice iteration but nothing mandatory unless you're already a fan of Assassin's Creed (which I am).

collection.name: Assassin's Creed
collection.review: There are few games that I've enjoyed as much as Assassin's Creed. Graphics and animation are top notch and the Third Crusade setting is very intriguing. You get to meet King Richard Lionheart, a shame that Saladin is only mentioned but never seen. Blending historical facts with fiction gives weight to the story which is very good. Although I can agree that its a bit repetitive it didnt matter to me at all, since I had too much fun running on rooftops, climbing towers and assassinating guards.

collection.name: Fallout: A Post Nuclear Role Playing Game
The Last of Us Part I
Total War: Shogun 2 - Fall of the Samurai
Mass Effect
collection.review: Totally epic, what a game! As a whole its a perfect blend between tactical shooting and role playing. All packaged with a very strong and fascinating story, gorgeous graphics and evocative music. The definitive space game, cant wait to play part 2 in the series!

collection.name: Mass Effect 3
collection.review_title: Very good in both single- and multiplayer
collection.review: An excellent game that concludes the Shepard storyline. Both graphics, music and gameplay are very good. The missions really take hold of you and they feel important to complete. Some decisions that you have to make are engaging as well. And I must be the only one in the universe that liked the ending.

collection.name: Mass Effect 2
collection.review:
After playing through Mass Effect I thought it was impossible to top it. But in many ways Mass Effect 2 is even better:
+ Better graphics
+ Gameplay is faster and even more exciting
+ Better side missions
+ More interesting companions
However:
- Main story is not as gripping as the first one. Its still good though.
- Equipment system too "dumbed down". Hard to know which weapons to use without numbers :(

This is still a fantastic game however, one of my all-time favourites!

collection.name: Zork II: The Wizard of Frobozz
Zork Zero: The Revenge of Megaboz
Beyond Zork: The Coconut of Quendor
The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy
World of Warcraft
collection.review: I played Wow for about 6 years and that must say something about the quality of this game. The world is really inviting and just plain fun to explore when you're new. For every patch and expansion pack there are some things that get better and some things that get worse. At the time of writing, the current expansion is Cataclysm. In the story department this expansion beats the others with the fantastic starting campaigns for worgen and goblins. The new quests between lvl 80-85 are also very good, especially in Uldum. Single player has become too easy now though, I almost never die or have to be careful and thats a shame. But raiding is much harder than in Wrath, albeit not as hard or inaccessible as in Vanilla wow. Bottom line is, I really like the humour and style of Wow.

collection.name: World of Warcraft: Wrath of the Lich King
World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade
Rayman 2: The Great Escape
collection.review: A very good platformer, if a bit dated. Should have received higher scores if it hadnt been for the ridiculous length between save points. Very annoying and stopped me from continuing the game, as I got too frustrated with all the backtracking.

collection.name: Age of Empires II: The Age of Kings
Neverwinter Nights 2: Mask of the Betrayer
Quest for Glory V: Dragon Fire
collection.review_title: A capable but slightly disappointing end for the series
collection.review: Uninspired compared to previous games in the series and I experienced a lot of bugs, including a game breaking one near the end (couldnt finish it). It still has some atmospheric and funny moments, enough for it to keep three stars. But it would have been best for this series to end with the excellent Shadows of Darkness.

collection.name: Hero's Quest: So You Want to Be a Hero
Quest for Glory II: Trial by Fire
Quest for Glory II: Trial by Fire
Quest for Glory III: Wages of War
Quest for Glory: Shadows of Darkness
Wallace & Gromit's Grand Adventures: Episode 2 - The Last Resort
The Lord of the Rings Online: Shadows of Angmar
Shroud of the Avatar: Forsaken Virtues

statuses.status: A really nice puzzler with a good sense of humour, never thought that goo balls could be cute before I played this! Overall a solid game that can be casually enjoyed but you can also go hardcore and complete all levels in OCD (Obsessive Completion Disorder) mode.

collection.name: Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space - Episode 5: What's New Beelzebub?
collection.review:
A satisfying conclusion and the overarching plot gets resolved. It was one of the better episodes, think this was about on par with episodes 1 and 4.

As a whole the series is a nice point and click but not extraordinarily good. Simply a good quality game with lots of funny comments from both Sam and Max as well as the supporting characters.

collection.name: Sam & Max: Save the World
collection.review_title: Some big hits and a few misses
collection.review: In the first season Sam and Max definitely loose their footing in some episodes but Reality 2.0 is the highlight of them all. I found that particular episode to be very funny and I like the whole homage to the VR craze in the early nineties. The little text adventure experiment was great fun too! Abe Lincoln must die is also a funny episode with an unexpected musical number thrown in. Sometimes it gets boring and repetitive but the above highlights make up for it.

collection.name: Dear Esther
collection.review_title: A nice experience, but too unfocused
collection.review: Dear Esther is not a game, its more like an experience in the same vein as The Path or Journey. Journey was fantastic, but I found The Path horrible. Dear Esther finds itself somewhere in between but closer to the Journey. The island is very beautiful and pleasant to explore and espescially the cave is very well done. I found the plot a bit too hard to grasp but I think I understood the main points. Overall Dear Esther is a nice experience but not as plot driven or emotional as I expected it to be.

collection.name: Call of Duty: Black Ops
collection.review: If you want a fast paced, gorgeous looking multiplayer game where you can frag your friends, this is the way to go. However, innovation is about zero. And since I dont get a kick out of killing and getting killed over and over, I got bored quickly and realised that this is just not my kind of game.

collection.name: Baldur's Gate II: Throne of Bhaal
collection.review: A very good but still slightly disappointing end to the Baldur's gate series. I had to play it to find the conclusion of the game series but I found it rushed and slightly silly. Suprisingly the Watchers Keep dungeon is the highlight of this expansion pack.

collection.name: Baldur's Gate II: Shadows of Amn
collection.review: Baldur's Gate 2: Shadows of Amn is the best part of the Baldur's Gate series. The game is not as open ended as the first one but this allows for a better story. Many hours of fun are found here and for each battle countless different strategic options can be used. A great followup to a timeless classic!

collection.name: Baldur's Gate
collection.review: The beginning of the 90's saw one of the best game releases ever, Origin's Ultima VII games. I found them fantastic and waited for many years for a game that could match them. With Baldur's Gate I finally found that game! While the story is weaker and too dark for my taste, the game is still lots of fun. The game interface is very intuitive and easy to use. It follows the Advanced Dungeons and Dragons rules but still manages to have exciting combat. Characters are diverse and have lots of dialogue. And depending on which partners you choose your gaming experience will become very different. This was a groundbreaking game for its time and it is still fun to play today.

collection.name: Indigo Prophecy
collection.review:
This is a fantastic interactive movie from the director of Heavy Rain. Only downside is that the plot is rushed towards the end but that shouldnt stop you from experiencing it. There are a couple of scares but where the game really shines is in its ability to mix true emotion with cool action sequences. Graphics are ok but they are dated by todays standards. But the soundtrack by Angelo Badalementi never ages. The music fits perfectly and is definitely on par with his previous work in Twin Peaks and Mulholland Drive. Most of the gameplay focuses on "Simon Says" sequences where you have to push buttons in the correct order. Sounds boring but I really liked it, they made me feel like I was part of the action.

Any fans of adventure games or good suspense movies should give Indigo Prophecy a try.

collection.name: Baldur's Gate: Tales of the Sword Coast
collection.review: This game gives you more of Baldur's Gate goodness, but to be honest I cant remember much of a story from this one. I do remember that the dungeons were quite nice and offered a challenge though.

collection.name: Gabriel Knight: Sins of the Fathers
Nine Hours, Nine Persons, Nine Doors
Trine
collection.review: A very good platformer in a fantasy setting. Trine brings some cool stuff for the table. For example you can conjure boxes and planks as the wizard and use them to drop on enemies or to jump on. As a thief you have a bow and a grappling hook for some crazy acrobatics. The fighter does the hack-n-slashing as well as throwing heavy objects. And you play them all at once, hotswapping to each character as needed! The music is very good and the graphics are gorgeous. Only downside was that I found it hard to get good precision when jumping, so it got slightly frustrating at times. But maybe thats just me.

collection.name: Defense Grid: The Awakening
collection.review_title: THE Tower Defense game to play!
collection.review: So far the best tower defense game I've played. The units feel powerful and its very pleasing to see them pulverize the aliens. Graphics and sound are so well done that it becomes a very immersive game. Base difficulty is quite easy but there is a challenge here for everyone. If you got friends playing the game it can be very addicting to try and beat their results in the leaderboards. Every level also got many different modes you can try for variation The AI voice is fantastic and really adds to the immersion. To sum up, fantastic value and a must buy!

collection.name: I Have No Mouth, and I Must Scream
Trauma
collection.review_title: Better than I thought it would be
collection.review: I enjoyed the mood in this game, the gestures and that it tries to do something different. Its very short (30-60 mins) but probably shouldnt be longer. There are a couple of minuses: The voices are not good, and the dialogue is probably meant to be deep and thoughtful but is just bad. If you can get it on sale its worth trying out.

collection.name: Magicka
collection.review: I havent had this much fun in a game for a long time. Magicka is both innovative and funny. Didnt notice any bugs, except the spell called "Crash to Desktop" ;) After a while I ended up using only a couple of spells though and it got a bit boring. Its also very frustrating to try and play this as a single player. Bring a friend and you'll have twice the fun!

collection.name: Worlds of Ultima: The Savage Empire
Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade: The Graphic Adventure
Layton's Mystery Journey: Katrielle and the Millionaire's Conspiracy
Orwell: Keeping an Eye on You
Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty
Metal Gear Solid 4: Guns of the Patriots
collection.review: A quite silly stealth action game. Since I've never played a MGS game before I didn't connect to the characters that much. I felt the cutscenes dragged on for too long with uninteresting details. The gameplay itself is better, but I had more fun sneaking around in Assassin's Creed. To be fair they are totally different games but this one never stuck on me.

Amnesia: The Dark Descent
collection.review_title: As scary as they say it is!
collection.review: I had high expectations for Amnesia: The Dark Descent and it didnt disappoint. It is very creepy, I had to play in slight chunks since the game really did scare me at certain points. The pacing is very good with a nice mix of story elements, escaping monsters, solving puzzles and having flashbacks. Recommended for anyone who wants a good scare and is able to play a game without any weapon in your hands!

collection.name: Edge
collection.review_title: Good but not great puzzle platformer
collection.review: A quite original platform/puzzle hybrid. Very similar in style to RUSH, which were made by the same people. You are a cube walking trying to find its way to the goal. There wasnt much thinking involved compared to previous titles from Two Tribes, which disappointed me slightly.

collection.name: Vampire: The Masquerade - Shadows of New York
Circle of Blood
collection.review_title: One of the best classic point and clicks!
collection.review:
*THIS REVIEW IS FOR THE IOS DIRECTORS CUT VERSION*

Im happy to say that point'n'click adventure games in general work really well on the smart phone, Broken Sword being no exception! For those that havent played the original, Broken Sword features George Stobbart and Nicole as they try to hunt down a killer but get ensared into a treasure hunt that involves the Knights Templar. The subject was very original in the middle of the 90's but post Da Vinci Code and all its followers it feels a bit cliched. It's still a strong story well worth a playthrough for adventure game fans!This director's cut also includes game segments with Nicole's investigation that was not included in the original game.

collection.name: Broken Sword: The Smoking Mirror
collection.review: A good game, but the first Broken Sword is better. The humour, excellent graphics and music is still there. But the story is not as good. Anyone who likes old school adventure games will still appreciate it overall. NOTE: The remastered edition does not offer any new story content like the Directors Cut of Broken Sword.

collection.name: Cave Story
collection.review: When I was a kid, neither me nor my friends owned a Nintendo. We had to try Super Mario Bros in the toy store. Thus I've never had much of a connection with old Nintendo games like Zelda or Castlevania. Cave Story+ is a game made to look and feel just like them. It's charming but not really up my alley. Its a nice game to play by its own merits though, once you customize the weird controls. Or just plug in a joypad. I have only gotten into a portion of the story as I write this but so far its nice with cute little rabbits ala Alice in Wonderland. Old Nintendo DS fans who want some nostalgia coupled with a fresh experience should give this a try!

collection.name: Outer Wilds: Echoes of the Eye
Wallace & Gromit's Grand Adventures: Episode 3 - Muzzled!
Detective Grimoire: Secret of the Swamp
Conquests of the Longbow: The Legend of Robin Hood
Twinsen's Little Big Adventure Classic
collection.review: Totally fantastic game that holds up incredibly well to this day. This is probably due to the unique art direction design. Fantastic story and music as well. If you're looking for a VERY different kind of action-adventure thats incredibly charming too, dont look any further!

collection.name: Sins of a Solar Empire: Rebellion
Lara Croft and the Guardian of Light
Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Dry Twice
Leisure Suit Larry: Wet Dreams Don't Dry
Altitude
collection.review: Altitude is a a quick and deceptively easy multiplayer game. Teamwork is essential to beat the other team. This is one of the games where I just continued playing and before I knew it, three hours had passed! I'm generally not a fan of multiplayer games, but this one was nice.

collection.name: Ori and the Will of the Wisps
Heavy Rain
collection.review:
Since I played Indigo Prophecy (Fahrenheit) and loved it, it's really no surprise that I was totally blown away by this title as well. After all, its from the same brilliant writer/director David Cage. Unfortunately, Indigo Prophecy suffered from a rushed and incomplete second part. With Heavy Rain, on the other hand, it's the second part of the plot that really shines. I thought I had it all figured out and definitely didnt see the twist that was coming! The story and setting is inspired by the landmark movie "Se7en": its raining all the time, a serial killer is on the loose and there are a lot of tough moral decisions for the characters involved. But its different enough to make it feel unique and not like a ripoff.

The graphics are really good and there must have been alot of work to create so many detailed locations. The characters faces are very detailed and it adds to the authencity. Music is good, but I was so immersed in the game that I didnt notice it much. Gameplay is mostly about choosing dialogue options and pressing the correct buttons when they show up. While it may sound simple, for me it was quite hard since I'm new to the PS3 controller. I took the medium difficulty and got to a "happy" ending, although one of the playable characters died. And here is one feature that I think is unique to Heay Rain: even though your character can die, there are no "Game Over" screens! The story continues without him/her and the ending of the game changes. I had read about all that before I played and didnt think much of it. But when my character died, a sense of failure washed over me. Before I started Heavy Rain I had decided to never reload and at that time it was very hard not to do so.
When the other characters got into trouble later on I was more determined to save them, since I wouldn't get a second chance. It was truly immersive and I can recommend to play the game this way.

All in all, Heavy Rain is an incredible interactive drama! I have only finished it once but will definitely replay it and make different choices next time around.

collection.name: Age of Conan: Unchained
collection.review:
This review only covers the Tortage leveling from 1-20 as I only did that part.

I never got around to endure the notorious bad launch of Age of Conan, since my computer didnt measure up. Since its now free to play, I decided to give the starting region a go. And I was pleasantly surprised. I didnt experience any bugs whatsoever, graphics are beautiful and the storyline is engaging. I've never liked the Conan universe before but here its not as over the top as the movies. I'd say this seems like a decent MMOs, better and more original than later ones such as Rift and Forsaken World.

collection.name: The Dark Pictures Anthology: Man of Medan
Game of Thrones: A Telltale Games Series
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Dual Destinies
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Spirit of Justice
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Trials and Tribulations
Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney - Justice for All
Limbo
collection.review: Limbo is a short and atmospheric puzzle platformer. There were a few shock moments involving a giant spider but except that it just feels dark and foreboding. You will die many times in a gorish fashion. Fortunately the save points are many so it never gets frustrating. The puzzles are often clever and I admit I had to check Youtube a couple of times when I got stuck. Well worth a playthrough!

collection.name: Ultima: Worlds of Adventure 2 - Martian Dreams
Star Wars: The Old Republic
collection.review:
A very good MMO, the class stories are definitely exciting and makes leveling a fun experience. I also had alot of fun with PvP. Regarding instances: the first instance for each faction is very good (Black Talon/Esseles), the others are ok but nothing extraordinary. Sound and graphics are excellent, it really feels like a Star Wars universe. A couple of small things annoyed me though. Firstly, since the world is so huge it can sometimes be tedious to move around. Second, some the side quests can be boring and feels like filler. Id rather just play the class stories if I could. Overall though, this is a fantastic game! I quit playing The Old Republic only because it took too much of my time and I couldn't put the the game down!

Disclaimer I never got to the endgame with operations so these opinions are only based on the levelling process and multiplayer. I mainly played a Sith Warrior, Bounty Hunter and Imperial Agent.

collection.name: Audiosurf
collection.review: I would love to give Audiosurf a good review, since the ability to build racing tracks that fit my own music is intriguing. But unfortunately I feel like I need to puke after only 10 minutes of this. All the weird colours and spiraling in the background just becomes too much. And a game that makes me sick simply cant get a good score! Am I the only one with this problem?

collection.name: Company of Heroes: Tales of Valor
Wing Commander III: Heart of the Tiger
Secrets of the Ark: A Broken Sword Game
Ultima Underworld II: Labyrinth of Worlds
King of Dragon Pass
collection.review: More reading than playing but the texts are of very good quality. Strategy elements are very deep but the rules are not shown so its best to go on instinct. Reading the manual is strongly recommended, you'll be rewarded for it. One of my favourites! Ideally you should get the iOS/Android version though. Its the "directors cut" and contains slightly more content as well as a superior interface.

collection.name: The Darkside Detective: A Fumble in the Dark
Monkey Island 2: LeChuck's Revenge
collection.review:
*This review covers the special edition released in digital stores*

First the good news - LucasArts did a much better job with this Special Edition than the one for The Secret of Monkey Island. The new graphics are beautiful and the interface has improved so much that I dont want to switch to classic mode much at all. They also included bonus stuff like concept art and funny commentaries from the authors of the original game (Ron Gilbert, Dave Grossman, Time Schafer) which is a really nice touch. The bad news - I realised that the witty dialog just isnt matched in the game design. Many puzzles just doesnt make sense and often feel contrived and not part of the main storyline. Why would Guybrush want to win a spitting contest in order to find Big Whoop for example? There are also "puzzles" for people who like to randomly try all inventory objects on everything until something succeeds ("monkey wrench" anyone?). In the original version pointless puzzles like these could be omitted in a "casual" mode. I must be the only one who liked the
casual mode better, since its not included in this special edition. I had previously rated this game a 5 for nostalgic reasons but the design issues above made me lower it to a 4. Still a classic though, well worth a playthrough.

collection.name: Journey
collection.review: Visuals in Journey are fantastic and I like that it feels like an experience more than a game. The "co-op" aspect was also a nice surprise, probably the most unintrusive multiplayer I've experienced. Since you're unable to chat with each other you instead focus on the task at hand. Overall, this was short but oh so sweet!

collection.name: Burnout Paradise
collection.review: A racer that I liked better than most. The sandbox approach felt a bit like the Grand Theft Auto games, in a positive way! It was a fun to explore the huge city and complete missions and upgrade my cars along the way.

collection.name: Agent A: A Puzzle In Disguise
Getting Over It with Bennett Foddy
Tales of Monkey Island: Chapter 3 - Lair of the Leviathan
Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse - Episode 5: The City That Dares Not Sleep
Max Payne
collection.review: I got lots of enjoyment from Max Payne it even though its ten years old by now. Its got a really cinematic feel and the story will keep you hooked to the end. Also really like the graphic novel format for the story.

collection.name: The Secret of Monkey Island
collection.review:
*This review is for the special edition found in digital stores*

I played through this game one more time and got surprised how good it still is today, 20 years later. Now we get an enhanced edition with the awesome feature that let you "hotswap" between the classic and the new version. It's very cool! However, I feel that there are some minor flaws in the enhanced edition that keeps it from getting the full grade:

-Not possible to skip single dialogs. Enhanced edition only lets you skip whole cutscenes, very annoying! I actually sometimes switch to classic mode which has the ability to let you skip single dialogs.
-No speech in classic mode. The voicework is great! Which makes it a shame that the speech is not enabled in the classic version. Everytime I hotswap I wish that they could just let speech stay on.
-Animation is quite ugly in new version, it actually looks better in the old one!

The classic version is a true 5 star game.

collection.name: Thimbleweed Park
collection.review:
This is a point and click adventure that feels just like a classic LucasArts game. That is no surprise, since the project is headed by Ron Gilbert, the Monkey Island and Maniac Mansion creator. 

What surprised me the most is that even though I didn't find the game very funny, it didn't hurt my experience at all. It's instead quite charming and has more than a few heart warming moments. The puzzles are just the right level of difficulty on Hard for seasoned adventure gamers. And for newcomers there is a Casual mode that makes things less frustrating. Another thing that surprised me is that this is not a small adventure game, it's really long but I never got bored! I replayed Monkey Island 1 & 2 recently and none of them are longer than ten hours. Here I finished in at about 25 hours (exploring mostly everything) and even with a walkthrough I don't think I would have finished it in under 15 hours. There is lots of dialogue too good to skip through and there are many beautiful locations to explore. 

Something that did annoy me in the beginning was the constant fourth wall breaking. Characters make many comments about being in a game, that you don't have to save often like in Sierra adventures and so on. The longer I played, the more I liked these things though.

Overall I really recommend this game. The old adventure game magic is here in spades.

collection.name: Indiana Jones and the Fate of Atlantis
Shadow Tactics: Blades of the Shogun
Agatha Christie: Hercule Poirot - The First Cases
Agatha Christie: The ABC Murders
collection.review:
A relaxing and fun detective game! The puzzles are quite simple but that is actually a plus since they are always logical! I also like the system where you make Poirots deductions. 

Even if there are a couple of mistakes I highly recommend this title to anyone who enjoys point and click adventures.

collection.name: Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons
Super Meat Boy
collection.review: Super Meat Boy is hard! Its not forgiving in the least and the slightest mistake will kill you. And you will die, many times. Its a fast paced platformer with some silly fun but for me it got frustrating after a while. For the really skilled players who are tired of noobs making "their" games too easy, this game is for you! For me it was fun for a while but was more punishing than fun in the end.

collection.name: Machinarium
collection.review: Machinarium is a cute game with cool art design and nice music. Its got a couple of innovative ideas, for example you can change the size of the main character and solve puzzles that way. Also there is no spoken dialogue, which is a positive thing and adds to the cartoony style. Other than that though, its a very traditional adventure game with some Myst-like puzzles thrown into the mix. Personally I found the puzzles too hard in the later sections and I often banged my head against the wall before I gave in and looked at hints.

collection.name: The Dark Eye: Chains of Satinav
Braid
collection.review: Braid is certainly a groundbreaking game with lots of fresh gameplay and a fantastic soundtrack. I have to admit that I found some of the puzzles hard to solve and had to check up solutions on youtube several times. Not sure if thats a good thing or not. Braid got very close to a 5 star rating, but unfortunately I think the story is a weak point of the game. I found it too complicated, pretentious and hard to follow. That's unfortunate, since the ending is incredibly powerful and well done.

collection.name: The Legend of Kyrandia 2: The Hand of Fate
Lands of Lore: Guardians of Destiny
Lands of Lore: The Throne of Chaos
Shatter
collection.review: I really liked Shatter. If you've ever liked Arkanoid/Breakout-style games you'll love this! Its action packed, with good graphics and music. You get special powers, most prominently you have a magnetic field that can either detract or attract objects as you wish. That and powers that change ball characteristics really spices up the old and tried formula. There are also lots of fun boss battles. A solid little 5 star game!

collection.name: The Journeyman Project 2: Buried in Time
Gris
collection.review: This might just be the best game I've ever played. Even though you can't die its constantly interesting gameplay, as new abilities are added over time and combined. The game look fabulous, what a work of art! The music is relaxing and feels completely integrated in the game. Story is not at the forefront but by the end a tear still came to my eye. For everyone who wants a relaxing, rewarding experience.

collection.name: Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse - Episode 2: The Tomb of Sammun-Mak
Magic: The Gathering - Duels of the Planeswalkers
collection.review: From the two hours I tried this game I learned that I don't like Magic the Gathering and especially not this plain version of it.

collection.name: Puzzle Agent
collection.review: Really enjoyed the story in this game, it's a perfect mix between Fargo and Twin Peaks. The 30+ puzzles presented in the game are generally easy but I still had lots of fun solving them.

collection.name: Bit.Trip Runner
collection.review: It feels like a rhythm game diguised as a platformer. A novel idea with some cool retro graphics and music. But it gets more frustrating than fun very quickly, since there are NO checkpoints. Fail once and you start the level all over again. And the last level is so long that it can only be masochists that want to finish it (I gave up).

collection.name: Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space - Episode 3: Night of the Raving Dead
collection.review:
One of the weaker episodes in this season, but still quite funny! I liked the disco puzzles but cant remember much of the episode otherwise.

As a whole the series is a nice point and click but not extraordinarily good. Simply a good quality game with lots of funny comments from both Sam and Max as well as the supporting characters.

collection.name: How to Cope with Boredom and Loneliness
King and Assassins: The Board Game
The Path
collection.review: I'm an adventure game fan and can appreciate art, so I had high hopes for this title. Unfortunately I was majorly disappointed. The biggest problem is that there is nothing interesting in the game world that makes you to keep playing! I was utterly bored and that is very uncommon when playing a game for me.

collection.name: To the Moon
collection.review_title: I cried two times while playing this
collection.review: To the Moon is a stunning interactive story, incredibly clever and also very emotional. The story and feel of the game is similar to the movie "Eternal Sunshine of the Spotless Mind". It is very short (around 4hrs) but dont let this discourage you. The music is fantastic, I bought the soundtrack right after I finished the game! Kan Gao, the mastermind behind To the Moon, is clearly very talented and I'll buy anything he makes after this! Anyone who appreciates a good interactive story MUST buy this game, period.

collection.name: Superbrothers: Sword & Sworcery EP
collection.review: This game has been very hyped and I do think it is overrated. Art direction is nice and music is fabulous. I also like their casual approach, in that they enourage you to take breaks. But the adventure elements themselves are not great. Some things do not work at all. The moon phases are horrible, I want to play when I want and not wait for the moon. The cave trick may work but is easy to fail and you end up with much backtracking. And changing the system clock is just so immersion breaking. Its best to play this on IPhone/IPad as the gestures are more effective on a touchscreen.

collection.name: Final Fantasy Tactics: The War of the Lions
Bullet Candy
collection.review: good arcade shooter with some fun extra powers to unlock! I suck at these kind of games though :)

collection.name: Delve Deeper
collection.review: I thought I would like this title, as Im a fan of both turn based strategy and rpg. However it soon becomes tiring to watch all the teams make their moves in single player. The game design looks like its made for multiplayer. But I could only find hot seat multiplayer which kinda ruins that part. Shame on such a promising game.

collection.name: Jamestown: Legend of the Lost Colony
Age of Wonders II: The Wizard's Throne
Alien Swarm
collection.review: This is a good top-down shooter in the Alien Breed style, with focus on multiplaying. It doesnt last long but hey, it free!

collection.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People Episode 2: Strong Badia the Free
Frog Detective 2: The Case of the Invisible Wizard
The Raven: Legacy of a Master Thief
BioForge
collection.review: I remember that this game was influenced alot by Alone in the Dark and featured similar gameplay but with a totally different cyberpunk setting. I found graphics to be gorgeous and the game as a whole was enjoyable. Not sure if it holds up today though, have to replay it at some point.

collection.name: Back to the Future: The Game - Episode 4: Double Visions
collection.review: Unfortunately, this chapter in the Back To The Future series wasn't as good as the others. The story mainly focuses on making Edna break up with Doc to prevent the Citizen Brown timeline. Its not intriguing and the puzzles are mostly tedious. It does set up the final episode nicely and hopefully that one will return to the higher quality of the previous episodes.

collection.name: Burn Zombie Burn!
collection.review: It becomes repetitive too quick, and the controls are awful for PC if you dont get a gamepad.

collection.name: Max Payne 2: The Fall of Max Payne
collection.review: A game as good as the first one, if not even better. Kinda liked Max better before but here the story is better developed and controls have been improved. It took me about 8 hours to finish this wonderful game. With such high intensity and superb production values, I dont find that too short.

collection.name: Orcs Must Die!
collection.review: Fun game, set traps and shoot/slash orcs as they try to reach the rift you are assigned to protect. Overall a funny and slightly different take on the tower defense genre. I just hope that they allow autofire on the crossbow, my finger gets numb from all the clicking!

collection.name: Wallace & Gromit's Grand Adventures: Episode 4 - The Bogey Man
Police Quest: In Pursuit of the Death Angel
Ken Follett's The Pillars of the Earth
Darkest Hour: A Hearts of Iron Game
Tales of Monkey Island: Chapter 1 - Launch of the Screaming Narwhal
Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse - Episode 1: The Penal Zone
Alien Breed 2: Assault
collection.review: Its kinda ok, but the game genre is not my style. Game is a simple arcade style shooter from a top down perspective. Story is silly but the point of this game is to shoot aliens, not to experience any Citizen Kane drama. Graphics are good but controls are a bit clunky, espacially when trying to change camera view. If you like these Alien Breed games but want better co-op, check out Alien Swarm (which is free on Steam).

collection.name: Mountain
collection.review: I'd label this an interactive screensaver, not a game. But whether its a game or not does not matter, as long as its immersive and entertaining. Mountain is none of these things. It's designed to run in the background or on your smartphone while your busy doing other things. The weather changes and random things and thoughts pop up. I never got the feeling that I cared about my mountain at all though. maybe these "caring" Tamagochi simulators are simply not for me.

collection.name: Heroine's Quest: The Herald of Ragnarok
Tiny Tina's Assault on Dragon Keep: A Wonderlands One-shot Adventure
And Yet It Moves
collection.review: My first impression of And Yet It Moves (silliest game name ever?) was a very positive one! The game mechanic, where you rotate the whole environment as well as the character, felt unique and fun. I soon got a bit bored though, since there is not much incentive to continue and beat the game. There is no story (that I discovered anyway) and environments dont differ much between the levels. Worth a try if it comes in a bundle or something.

collection.name: The Legend of Kyrandia 3: Malcolm's Revenge
Phantasmagoria
collection.review:
When Phantasmagoria was released I bought the game but it bugged out when I tried to play it. It always annoyed me that I couldn't play it but now I finally was able to after buying it on GOG.com.
Roberta Williams wrote Phantasmagoria. The main character explores a house with many secrets and fans who have played her older games Mystery House and Colonel's Bequest will feel right at home! But with one noticeable difference, this time the place is haunted! Phantasmagoria succeeds on many levels: the story is very intriguing and the atmosphere is great. The game is also manage to start out as slightly creepy and only gets more frightening as the chapters pass by. Gameplay is easy but that was fine with me. In this case it works since I didn't want any overly complicated puzzles to ruin the immersion. Graphics were gorgeous back then but it feels outdated now. There was a lot of work on details around the house and this adds to the positive experience.
In short, if you're into adventure games and horror you don't want to miss this great game.

collection.name: Prince of Persia 2: The Shadow and the Flame
Labyrinth City: Pierre the Maze Detective
Sam & Max: Save the World - Episode 4: Abe Lincoln Must Die!
Telltale Texas Hold'em
collection.review: Telltale Texas Hold'Em is actually a fun way to learn the rules of Texas Hold'em Poker if you don't know them. But once you've played a couple of hours and get tired of the comments its more fun to play against real opponents.

collection.name: Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse - Episode 4: Beyond the Alley of the Dolls
Faerie Solitaire
collection.review: This game is relaxing to play for a while when you just need 30 minutes of brain dead clicking (like in my case when the kids wake you up at 5 in the morning and you need to do something to stay awake). Music tunes in the background are soothing and its nice that they wrapped a story, pets and collectibles around the card games as well to keep you going. Oh, and trying to get combos is addictive! Solitaire never gets better than this.

collection.name: Blade Runner
collection.review: This was a game that I had in my shelf for a looong time but I only got around to play it recently. And what a pleasant surprise! This game is beautiful and catches the Blade Runner setting perfectly. The story is similar to the movie but still manage pull a few surprises on its own. Its definitely just not a movie ripoff. Puzzle elements were nice and I was excited during the whole playthrough. Multiple endings add to the replay value.

collection.name: Tales of Monkey Island: Chapter 5 - Rise of the Pirate God
LEGO The Lord of the Rings
Rift
collection.review: Rift is kinda nice, it plays along nicely without bugs and its kinda cool that its easy to join Rift battles. Overall its an ok game, but nothing spectacular. The story didnt impress me much though, and it quickly felt like a grind. I still find World of Warcraft to be a superior MMO.

collection.name: Heroes of Might and Magic II: The Succession Wars
collection.review: This was a game that literally hooked me in front of the computer for days back in the 90's, when I was a student! Heroes 3 is still the superior version, but this second installation has a charm on its own. This game is similar to Warlords with a touch of RPG to it. Build armies, lead your heroes and conquer your foes! Its childens cartoon like graphics were nothing impressive even back then but its still playable. The music is very charming and one of my all time favorites! The other day I played the demo of Heroes 6 I was surpised at how little the game series has evolved since Heroes 2. If you're just into Heroes for the single player you can just as well pick up number 2 or 3 instead of 6. They're all good (well, I've not played 1 & 4 so cant comment on these), but 2 & 3 are my favorites!

collection.name: Wing Commander IV: The Price of Freedom
Back to the Future: The Game - Episode 5: Outatime
collection.review:
A fitting end to the series. After the fourth episodes everything was so confused that I thought they were gonna mess the ending up. Im happy to say they didnt, all loose ends were tied up. The disappointing fourth episode was just a setback, here the puzzles make sense and I was always motivated to push ahead. The voice acting is fantastic throughout the series but now the cast was completed with Michael J Fox himself! It was a fantastic surprise and it also showed what an incredibly good job A.J. Locascio does as the voice of Marty. He sounds exactly like a younger version of Michael! There were a couple of bugs and even one that affected gameplay, which was mildly annoying. However, since this episode had more exciting moments than any previous episode, Im generous and give OUTATIME the full 5 stars.

My grade for the whole series is 4 stars. Recommended for fans of the franchise!

collection.name: Elegy for a Dead World
collection.review_title: Like to write? Try this for something different!
collection.review:
This is more of an fun educational tool than a game since it's all about trying to get you, the player, to write! You can explore three beautiful worlds inspired by Byron, Keats and Shelley and then you try to write about these worlds! There are several different writing templates available or you can just write without one of course. Personally I liked to start with a template but change the text in it as I went, eventually ending up with something that was mainly my own story. 

The negative thing I can say is that the integration with the Steam Workshop could have been better. It would have been nice if I could've read other user's stories more easily directly in the workshop without having to be in the game. But as a whole I'd recommend Elegy For a Dead World to anyone who wants a little nudge to get their creative minds flowing!

collection.name: Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People Episode 4: Dangeresque 3 - The Criminal Projective
2000:1 - A Space Felony: Or How I Came to Value My Life and Murder Mercilessly
Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space - Episode 1: Ice Station Santa
collection.review:
Bad santas are always funny and this is a strong start of the second season but its nothing out of the ordinary. Expect a traditional adventure which is good but without much surprises.

As a whole the series is a nice point and click but not extraordinarily good. Simply a good quality game with lots of funny comments from both Sam and Max as well as the supporting characters.

collection.name: Spycraft: The Great Game
collection.review: This is a game that I had in my shelf for more than 10 years until I decided to start playing it. Graphics are outdated of course but many of the game elements are still very gripping today. The best thing about Spycraft is that it feels authentic in many parts, I felt like a CIA agent out on the field! The most outdated part are the shooting sequences but thankfully they are only a small portion of the game.

collection.name: Tex Murphy: Under a Killing Moon
Defender's Quest: Valley of the Forgotten
Windosill
collection.review: Its very short, for me it took less than an hour to go through the rooms. It a relatively high score anyway because its a very innovative game and physics based puzzles are fun to solve. Get it if its on a Steam sale.

collection.name: Arcanum: of Steamworks and Magick Obscura
The Last Express
collection.review:
This is a work of art. There are games out there with better gameplay but the atmosphere that they create in The Last Express is not like any other. Everything in the game feels authentic, from the recreated Orient Express to the performance of the characters. The characters are diverse and like in a good Agatha Christie novel, it feels like all of them got something to hide. A lot of small details add to the experience. For example you can pick up a paper and read about authentical historical events from 1914, when the game is set. Add an immersive story to the mix and you have a truly enjoyable game.

For a long time The Last Express has been very hard to get hold of, but now its available to download from gog.com for a cheap price. Any adventure gaming fan should play this!

collection.name: Tales of Monkey Island: Chapter 4 - The Trial and Execution of Guybrush Threepwood
Gemini Rue
collection.review:
A solid adventure game in retro style. Gemini Rue runs only in 320x200 resolution, so people who play games for good graphics should stay away. But people who enjoy a cool story in the style of Blade Runner should definitely give this one a look! Puzzles are not too hard, although I did look in a walkthrough at one point. For me that is a good thing, as I find it frustrating to solve overcomplicated puzzles that detracts from the story.
Gemini Rue was developed almost singe-handedly by Joshua Nuernberger, who studied at UCLA at the time. I find this to be quite incredible since it is easily comparable with many adventure games from the "good old days". Recommended!

collection.name: Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space - Episode 2: Moai Better Blues
collection.review_title: The banter between Sam and Max saves the day
collection.review:
The weakest episode in this season in my opinion. Didnt find it as funny as the others and there were a few puzzles that were overly complicated and dragged a bit. Ok but not more!

As a whole the series is a nice point and click but not extraordinarily good. Simply a good quality game with lots of funny comments from both Sam and Max as well as the supporting characters.

collection.name: Six Ages: Ride like the Wind
The Life and Suffering of Sir Brante
Dragon Quest XI: Echoes of an Elusive Age
Back to the Future: The Game - Episode 1: It's About Time
collection.review: The first episode in Telltales "Back To The Future" series sets up the story nicely and leaves you wanting more, while still containing a story on its own. The strongest part of the game is the production quality, this IS Back to the Future! Marty and Doc are still in character and graphics, music and voicework are outstanding. The weak part of this game series as a whole would be that there is not much challenge to be found here, but for a game with such nice production values it does not matter much for a real BttF fan like me.

collection.name: Sam & Max: Beyond Time and Space - Episode 4: Chariots of the Dogs
collection.review:
Time travel in space is fun! Chariots of the dogs is a classic time travelling episode with lots of original ideas. Of of the better episodes in the season for sure!

As a whole the series is a nice point and click but not extraordinarily good. Simply a good quality game with lots of funny comments from both Sam and Max as well as the supporting characters.

collection.name: Back to the Future: The Game - Episode 2: Get Tannen!
collection.review:
Excellent episode in Telltale's faithful version of Back To The Future. Here Marty and Doc needs to stop Kid Tannen from totally destroying Marty's future. The puzzles are fairly easy but since the story is good and a fun ride, it doesn't matter much. A couple of the solutions also feel original. For instance, at one point Marty have to change a person's mood to get the information he wants by changing the songs that he listens to.
Overall a very enjoyable couple of hours and ends in a nice cliffhanger for episode 3.

collection.name: Tesla Effect: A Tex Murphy Adventure
Back to the Future: The Game - Episode 3: Citizen Brown
collection.review:
This time Marty is in serious trouble, as usual! He has crashed the time machine and is now stuck in an alternate timeline! Too much time travelling makes my head spin so I like that he stays in the same place and time this whole episode. Just the setting of Doc and Edna overseeing a 1984-like (ok, it takes place in 1986) Hill Valley makes this episode original and fun. The episode takes about 2-3 hours to finish just like the previous episodes in the series. Many people seem to want a longer game but I for one think that this is a perfect length for a game episode. Puzzles are easy but that doesn't matter since the story never gets boring and keeps you captivated all the way to the cliffhanger.

Voice acting is fantastic, with AJ Locascio doing commendable work as Marty. Telltale should be lucky that they found this up and coming voice talent! Christopher Lloyd has not as much to do in this episode unfortunately, personally I hope we get to see more of "old" Doc. His partnership with Marty is a classic one and feels just like in the movies (well, THIS particular episode might be an exception).

Bottom line is, you'll be happy as long as you don't expect a challenging game. This is more like a fun ride and a set of very good interactive movies. All who liked the original movies should get this game series, as the episodes just gets better and better.

collection.name: Geometry Wars: Retro Evolved
collection.review: A good retro arcade shooter no more, no less!

collection.name: Might & Magic: Clash of Heroes
collection.review: A game that is both great fun and original! The battle system is easy to learn but hard to master, as in any good game. I found the campaign to be surprisingly good and diverse. Its not just battles the whole time, they are mixed up with good puzzles and dialogue. I admit that I got a little bored half-way (Heresh) but then in Sheogh it picks up again and the final part of the campaign has some sweet surprises up its sleeve. If you like puzzle games and fantasy this is a must have!

collection.name: Wallace & Gromit's Grand Adventures: Episode 1 - Fright of the Bumblebees
Indiana Jones and the Emperor's Tomb
The Beast Within: A Gabriel Knight Mystery
Tales of Monkey Island: Chapter 2 - The Siege of Spinner Cay
Gabriel Knight 3: Blood of the Sacred, Blood of the Damned
Sam & Max: The Devil's Playhouse - Episode 3: They Stole Max's Brain!
The Captain
collection.review:
The Captain is a fantastic adventure game in many ways.

It's a game that both captures the Star Trek magic and the feel of classic adventures. Every planet is beautiful and full of charming details. I found all puzzles to be logical rather than frustrating and they a joy to play through. Some puzzles, like one where you have to meditate and find your Zen, are even groundbreaking. 

The writing of is of consistent high quality and is unexpectedly comical many times. A shuttle with an attitude(!) made me smile more than once. Those of you that have played the Space Quest games will feel right at home here. This game is vastly superior to the Space Quests though: no unexpected deaths, no cluttered inventories and some planets have quite touching, dramatic stories. Fenton Perth for example is a planet well worth visiting, more than once!

Besides Fenton Perth, there are a plethora of planets that you will want to visit more than once. Because The Captain is one of very few games that do choice and consequence right. Like the game "80 days", you travel on a map, visit places and experience relatively self contained events. This makes your choices very visual. You choose to visit some planets, but might have to skip others to save time. For many other games it has been a challenge to visualise choices. Some games (Witcher 2 for example) can have choices that completely alter the game without the player realising. Other games, like many from Telltale, give an illusion of choice where seemingly important choices don't change the outcome very much. Another good design choice in the Captain is to provide so called "ending cards". They serve two purposes: you can play the ending card to fast forward through parts of the game in a replay. The other purpose is to show the player where there is more content to be found and where you might want to go when replaying the game.

Not sure if I can find anything bad about The Captain really. It even has a surprisingly deep turn based battle system. Battles are completely optional but I found myself spending many hours killing pirates and upgrading my ship. There have been a few minor bugs but they have been promptly fixed by the devs. A fun fact is that this massive game was made by two friends over a period of five years!

Highly recommended, and well worth the full price!

collection.name: Simon the Sorcerer II: The Lion, the Wizard and the Wardrobe
Agatha Christie: Murder on the Orient Express

collection.review: A puzzle platformer who's relies on letting the music teach you how to play. The music is awesome and is the best reason for playing 140. It's very short, I finished it in a little more than an hour. It also varies alot in difficulty and can be frustrating from time to time. But the last "boss fight"/puzzle is brilliant!

collection.name: Sentinels of the Multiverse: The Video Game
King Arthur II: The Role-Playing Wargame
Bejeweled Blitz
collection.review: A nice alternative to Tetris-style game, but I still find Tetris to be more fun.

collection.name: The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening
Strong Bad's Cool Game for Attractive People Episode 1: Homestar Ruiner
Invictus: In the Shadow of Olympus
The King of Shreds and Patches
Wordfeud
collection.review: Very addicting Scrabble clone. Here in Sweden it has become immensely popular and pratically all people with smartphones are playing it in the tube on their way to work/school. Comes slightly short of the full score since the quality of the dictionary could be better.

collection.name: Hammerfight
collection.review: Whats best about Hammerfight is that its unique and innovative. I'm not sure if it actually works out though. It can be very pleasing to get a smashing blow with your hammer, but the tempo is so high so mostly I just turn the mouse around in circles like crazy and thats no fun. I didnt come too far into the story as difficulty ramps up too quickly.

collection.name: Touché: The Adventures of the Fifth Musketeer
collection.review_title: Tries to be Monkey Island but fails
collection.review: Touché is an old adventure game from the 90's that follows a guy who aspires to be a musketeer, much like how Guybrush Treepwood tries to be a pirate in The Secret of Monkey Island. Unfortunately its not anywhere near the quality of the Monkey Island games. Some jokes are funny but alot of them are not. Character models are reused and the locations feel similar to each other. collection.name: Blueberry Garden
collection.review: I was disappointed in Blueberry Garden, the gameplay was lacking in many aspects. It was hard to figure out what the berries actually did and no ability to save progress was annoying. After an hour I got tired of trying to "beat" the game and watched a YouTube video of the solution instead. Since the game won awards and generated some media buzz here in Sweden I expected more. Extra star for the lovely piano music though.

The puzzles are still good, even if they can be very easy sometimes.
